observations.summary: Mama was standing right next to Lucas when he said 'Mama!'. Papa told him Mama was right there. Lucas sometimes became quiet and sometimes continued saying 'Mama!'.
observations.interpretation: Open question; possible functions must not be treated as established.

observations.summary: After Papa showed a Super Mario 'Mamma mia!' short and asked if Lucas meant that, Lucas smiled and said 'Mamma mia!'.
observations.interpretation: Reported response to the phrase; does not prove intended meaning of earlier signal.

School reportedly sings a morning 'Bom dia' song. Lucas started singing it at home; on 9/24 reportedly sang a school song to Mama/attempted to teach or share it.
observations.interpretation: Reported carryover. Correct lyrics requested from teacher; no claim about mastery.

observations.summary: During Minecraft Creative play, Lucas produced many chicks and sang Five Little Ducks. Papa recognized it at 'quack quack'; other lyrics were difficult to hear.
observations.interpretation: Record as co-occurrence; avoid asserting a developmental pattern.

observations.summary: Old MacDonald Had a Farm also reported among songs Lucas sings; lyrics heard approximately as 'McDonald had a firm'.

Conversation reports “Shinansen” as a strong interest/repeated utterance; “No?” ↔ “Shinansen” as a functional pairing whose meaning is unexplained; and “sky is blue!”, “going out!”, “trees!” in relation to outings.
observations.interpretation: Literal meaning, personally extended function, and learned chunks may coexist. Any outing/access-signal interpretation is provisional.

observations.summary: Caregiver recalls a period of increasing new-word acquisition, followed after a while by apparent slowdown/stagnation; family instability was present during that period. Lisbon/outside stimulation was considered, and spouse reportedly stopped those outings.
observations.interpretation: Historical context and candidate hypotheses only. No causal relationships or developmental measurements are established.
